scope: MCP tool registration, input/output schemas, error handling and API contract consistency (src/mcp.ts, src/domain.ts, src/files.ts, src/security.ts, src/coordinator.ts, src/store.ts, src/http.ts, src/cli/client.ts, docs/MCP-API.md)

findings.title: Documented idempotent spawn_worker retry is rejected as 'different arguments' when the configured default timeout changes
findings.evidence: coordinator.spawn builds {...parsed, timeout_seconds: parsed.timeout_seconds ?? config.SWARMFORGE_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS} (src/coordinator.ts:185-190) and Store.create hashes JSON.stringify(input) including that server-chosen value (src/store.ts:71-74); a fingerprint mismatch raises 'request_id already used with different arguments' (src/store.ts:81-82) which register() returns as isError (src/mcp.ts:50-67). Contract: docs/MCP-API.md:29 and the tool description at src/mcp.ts:73.
findings.reproduction: Reproduced (exit 0) in /tmp/rv: two Coordinators over one Store(':memory:') with SWARMFORGE_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS 600 then 1200, driven through a linked MCP client/server pair; identical spawn_worker arguments + request_id produced {"isError":true,"text":"request_id already used with different arguments"}. Existing tests only retry with an unchanged config (tests/lifecycle.test.ts:6-19, tests/core.test.ts:87-114), so nothing covers this.
findings.recommendation: Hash and compare the caller-supplied Spawn (before the config default is applied), or persist the client arguments next to request_fingerprint and compare those; keep the default only as an effective value.

findings.title: spawn_worker returns the current state on a retry instead of the documented initial queued state
findings.evidence: The action echoes state: w.state from the stored worker (src/mcp.ts:71-84); Store.create returns the pre-existing worker on a fingerprint match (src/store.ts:79-84). docs/MCP-API.md:7 documents 'initial queued state'.
findings.reproduction: Reproduced (exit 0): first call {"state":"queued"}; same-args retry after one tick returned {"state":"booting"}. tests/lifecycle.test.ts:6-19 asserts only worker_id equality, never the returned state.
findings.recommendation: Document that a retry returns the current state and/or add an explicit created/duplicate flag so clients need not infer freshness from state.

findings.title: Input-schema violations are JSON-RPC -32602, not isError; the in-handler ZodError branch is unreachable and unredacted
findings.evidence: The MCP SDK validates the declared inputSchema before the callback, so the handler's z.ZodError -> 'Invalid tool arguments' branch (src/mcp.ts:38-68) can never fire, and that SDK path does not pass through redactor.text. docs/MCP-API.md:25 states 'Tool failures set isError'; src/cli/client.ts:31-50 only inspects isError.
findings.reproduction: Reproduced (exit 0): 18 invalid-argument cases across 8 tools all returned thrown JSON-RPC -32602 messages such as 'MCP error -32602: Input validation error: Invalid arguments for tool get_worker: ...'. In 6 targeted cases the message did not echo the offending value, so no secret escaped today; the redaction gap is structural.
findings.recommendation: Correct docs/MCP-API.md:25 to document the -32602 behaviour, remove the unreachable branch, and redact outgoing protocol error text (server error hook) for any future rule that could echo input.

findings.title: get_worker_artifact collapses every failure into one message and is the only tool that skips redaction and the response cap
findings.evidence: Bare catch {} returns 'Artifact unavailable or invalid path' for unknown workers, destroyed/VM-less workers, traversal, symlinks, credential-shaped paths (src/files.ts:5-10,11-22,32-40,70-71) and provider timeouts. Registered directly with server.registerTool (src/mcp.ts:181-224), so it also bypasses the redactor and 128 KiB cap applied by register() (src/mcp.ts:40-45). No live disclosure: files.artifact already refuses credential-shaped paths and the handle echoes only path/size/URI.
findings.reproduction: Reproduced (exit 0): {worker_id:'w-does-not-exist', path:'a.txt'} and {worker_id:'w-does-not-exist', path:'../escape'} returned the identical string. tests/api.test.ts:101-127 and 185-192 assert WorkerFiles rejections directly and never the tool's error text.
findings.recommendation: Map known WorkerFiles errors to stable machine-readable codes (or pass the redacted message, keeping one generic string only for traversal/symlink) and route this tool through register() so its output is redacted and size-capped.
